subject: SwiftMatch transition economics and limited-time match offer
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena@swiftmatch.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@swiftmatch.com
Date: 2027-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing ask + potential match (follow-up)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to share a baseline of our current spend and to see if Redwood can provide a time-limited match to keep us from going with another vendor. Attached is a simple workbook with our current ARR and token usage profile.

What we need:
- A 12-month blended rate that brings cost within ~10% of our incumbent (we've included the incumbent's effective price in the sheet)
- Clarity on what packaging (included requests, reserved throughput) is required for the price to hold
- Any migration credits or one-time professional services discounts to offset early termination fees

Can you confirm if Redwood can put together a 1-page counter with options (match, sweetener credits, 6 vs 12 month commitment)? Procurement is on a tight cadence — aim for something by Wednesday EOD if possible.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ortiz
Head of Cloud Ops, SwiftMatch

[attachment: swiftmatch_pricing_request.xlsx]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@swiftmatch.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ask + potential match (follow-up)

Elena — thanks for the file, that's helpful. Quick read: your token distribution spikes on weekly batch jobs and you have predictable steady-state user traffic. Two thoughts up front: 

1) We can approach this three ways: pure unit-price match (per-token), a blended reserved+burst package, or a hybrid with migration credits.
2) For a match inside 10% we will likely need a 12-month reservation for core capacity plus a small pilot discount to offset your early termination exposure.

I'm looping in Jordan for commercial packaging and Jasmine for migration ops. I'll put a short counter on paper and include an ops runbook so they can see migration work that reduces risk (helps with exec approval on your side).

I'll aim for a one-page options matrix by end of day tomorrow.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
AM, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ortiz <elena@swiftmatch.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@swiftmatch.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing ask + potential match (follow-up)

Rafael/Jasmine — draft commercial thoughts below, I put three discreet options with clear tradeoffs. Rafael, feel free to share directly with Elena as a starting point.

Option A — Unit-price match (fastest approval)- 12-month term, per-token price matched to incumbent for the blended volume in sheet- No reserved throughput required, burst limits shared; overages billed monthly- No migration credits; onboarding support included (2 weeks)

Option B — Reserved + pilot credit (recommended for cost predictability)- 12-month term with reserved capacity covering 75% of steady-state tokens at a 15% discount vs our list price- 3-month pilot credit equal to 10% of first-quarter spend to offset termination fees- Migration assistance (1 FTE week + runbook) and one-way data-transfer credits

Option C — Short commit with larger sweetener (lower risk for customer)- 6-month term, deeper upfront credit (20% of 6-month committed spend) to offset switching costs- Automatic rate review at month 5 for potential extension

Notes: all options assume SOC2 evidence review and basic ingress/egress support; pricing in sheet assumes NLS quantization-level 8 for inference. If they want GPU-reserved SLAs (Dedicated-like), we'd price that separately.

I'll attach a concise one-pager and a migration outline (Jasmine) after we confirm which option to present.

-Jordan
Sr. Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena@swiftmatch.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T13:01:00-07:00
Subject: Migration ops outline (attachment: migration_plan_v1.pdf)

Hi Elena — attaching a short migration plan and runbook (see migration_plan_v1.pdf). High-level:

- Week 0: Kickoff, environment access, data transfer protocol agreement- Week 1–2: Pilot (10% traffic) with mirrored routing, latency verification, token accounting validation- Week 3–4: Gradual cutover and SLA verification; dedicated on-call during cutover- Deliverable: Redlined SOW and final rollback playbook

We estimate 3–4 engineering days on your side for pilot validation; Redwood provides 2 engineer-weeks of migration support in the pilot credit line. If SwiftMatch needs a white-glove Dedicated environment, timeline extends by 1–2 weeks.

Attachments: migration_plan_v1.pdf

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@swiftmatch.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena@swiftmatch.com>
Cc: procurement@swiftmatch.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-17T09:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SwiftMatch pricing options — procurement questions

Team — procurement had three quick asks after reviewing the options:
1) Can you list the exact termination fee mitigation (how the pilot credit applies vs early termination)?
2) Are there any data retention or log-export charges we should budget for?
3) Legal wants a short example SOW with deliverables and acceptance criteria before signing.

Also: is the 10% window on the unit-price match negotiable if we commit to a 9-month plan instead of 12?

Thanks,
Tom
Senior Procurement Manager, SwiftMatch

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Keller <tom.keller@swiftmatch.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena@swiftmatch.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-17T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SwiftMatch pricing options — procurement questions

Tom — quick answers inline and next steps.

1) Termination mitigation: the pilot credit is applied as a one-time invoice credit against the first invoice after go-live; if SwiftMatch terminates within the first 90 days of go-live we will offset agreed early termination fees up to the amount of the pilot credit. We'll put exact language in the SOW (attached redlined-sow.docx once legal confirms).

2) Data retention/log export: no additional charges for standard log exports (30-day retention). Long-term export storage (S3/archival) billed at cost; we'll include an estimate in the one-pager.

3) SOW: will send a draft SOW that covers deliverables, acceptance criteria, rollback windows and liability caps. Jordan — can you approve the commercial bullets to include in the SOW?

On the 9-month question: we can consider a 9-month commit at a slightly higher effective unit price vs 12 months; propose we present both 9- and 12-month paths in the options matrix so SwiftMatch can choose their acceptable tradeoff.

I'll consolidate into one PDF and route a DocuSign link for signature once they pick a path. Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
